cards.issue_title: Loan-amount how-calculated steps have no names, so the chain cannot be followed
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, they opened Bank of Maharashtra’s loan-amount drawer.
The six steps show bare numbers (80%, 55%, 10%, ₹555) without names.
They could not tell what 80% or 55% was, or why the next step exists.
They said the steps must be sequenced and each number must have a name and label.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the Bank of Maharashtra loan-amount how-calculated drawer shows six numbered arithmetic steps whose percentages and leftover rupees (80.00%, 55.00%, 10.00%, −₹555) have no names, so a reader cannot follow why step n is useful or where 80/55/10 came from.
cards.on_screen_object: Loan amount drawer for Bank of Maharashtra · Maha Super Housing Loan (opened from ₹48,00,000 — Show how loan amount was calculated)
quotes_sample: So I don't know why the next step is useful.
Now he has done into 800. What is 800?
I need their names and labels.
related_discussion_one_liners: Called the loan amounts “amazing” / “we are getting a lot of loans” while still attacking the unlabeled math.
Accepted a single calculation if it is easy to follow.
Restated the intended chain: income allowance × FOIR − EMIs − credit-card load = monthly EMI eligibility; income limit 68 lakh; lower-of → 48 lakh.
Later reopened the same drawer as proof a bank agent only gets a system or head-office figure — praise of having the drawer, not a second defect.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the loan-amount drawer’s six unlabeled arithmetic steps (80%/55%/10%/−₹555 with no names or sequencing), not the EMI formula’s unnamed 12/0.006 and not the Charges footnote * vs ^ glyphs.

cards.issue_title: EMI how-calculated formula leaves 12 and 0.006 unnamed
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks they opened Bank of Maharashtra’s EMI drawer (₹37,938).
The formula shows 7.25% ÷ 12 and a bare 0.00604167 with no word “months” or “monthly rate”.
They asked why yearly interest is needed, why it says “into”, and what 0.06 is.
They still called showing EMI math revolutionary — that praise is not this issue.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the Bank of Maharashtra EMI how-calculated drawer prints 7.25% ÷ 12 = 0.6042% and then 0.00604167^(240) without labeling 12 as months or 0.00604167 as the monthly rate, so they could not read the formula.
cards.on_screen_object: EMI drawer for Bank of Maharashtra · Maha Super Housing Loan (opened from ₹37,938 — Show how EMI was calculated)
quotes_sample: I need to know that interest is monthly. I don't know why I need to calculate the annual interest.
It would have been better if it was written as months.
related_discussion_one_liners: Praised the existence of the explanation: “Very nice. Nobody knows how EMI is calculated. This is a revolutionary product.”
Said a branch agent does not know this much and only gets a system or head-office figure.
Joked about not having money at home.
Expected the drawer to open and slide-select on click — “Very nice.”
Said “we don't lie to the customer / we are here to empower you” as the reason this drawer should exist.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the EMI drawer’s formula leaving 12 and 0.00604167 unnamed (no “months” / “monthly rate”), not the loan-amount step names and not the Charges footnote * vs ^ / dash-as-link marks.

cards.issue_title: Charges footnote dash looks like a link; they want stars, and there is an extra mark
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks → Charges they looked at the * and ^ marks on fee column titles.
They said a dash is for linking and must not be used as a note mark.
They want a star, like Apple’s footnote marks, so notes are not confused with links.
They counted three index marks and only two stars — an extra mark is sitting there.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Charges, footnote marks on Processing fees / Property check / Government charges mix * and ^ (ASR: dash), which they said looks like a link rather than a note; they want stars, and they counted three indexes but only two stars — an extra mark.
cards.on_screen_object: Charges tab column-title note buttons: Processing fees *, Property check charges *, Government charges ^, plus Notes * / ^ blocks
quotes_sample: Actually there is an extra mark here.
related_discussion_one_liners: Apple analogy: Apple’s site uses many footnote marks but keeps them distinct from links; they said Apple underlines marks so people don’t get confused.
“Dash might look long” / “there are a lot of them.”
After the glyph talk they opened Indian Bank ₹2,500 processing-fee how-calculated with almost no remaining speech.
Next recording starts “what is a processing fee” on the same Charges / processing-fee note — note-body talk, not the glyph (belongs in 0004).
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is Charges footnote glyphs (* vs ^, dash looking like a link, three indexes vs two stars), not unlabeled loan-amount steps and not unlabeled EMI formula numbers.
